Getting help with cuplyr

Source: .github/SUPPORT.md

Thanks for using cuplyr. Before you file an issue, work through the steps below. They make the problem faster to fix.

Make a reprex

Start with a minimal reproducible example, made with the reprex package. If you haven’t used reprex before, the Get help! page on the tidyverse site explains it in a few minutes. Build the data inside the example, and say whether the table is eager or lazy.

Check your installation

Most first problems are installation problems. Run these and read the output:

cuplyr::verify_installation()
cuplyr::diagnostics()

Paste the output of diagnostics() into any bug report.

Where to ask

With your reprex ready, decide where to ask.

  • Questions go to forum.posit.co or Stack Overflow. More people can answer there.
  • Bugs go here. File an issue.
  • Not sure? File an issue anyway and say so.

Before you open a new issue, search issues and pull requests to check that the bug isn’t already reported or fixed in the development version. The search starts with is:issue is:open. Remove is:open to include closed issues.

What happens next

cuplyr has one maintainer, so a reply can take a few days. The maintainer starts by running your reprex, and a bug that can’t be reproduced can’t be fixed.
